claims.claim: A faster language would shrink 20 CPU-minutes to maybe 5–10 (i.e. Go, Rust or a JVM language would do the CPU work about 2–4x faster than Node)
claims.about: Node (Express) vs Go, Rust, JVM for CPU-bound work
claims.measured: CPU fib(20): node-express 7,213 req/s, node-fastify 8,308; go-gin 18,218 (~2.5x Express), rust-actix 26,886 and rust-axum 29,499 (~3.7–4x), java-spring 14,258 (~2x), kotlin-ktor 18,350 (~2.5x), cpp-drogon 35,839 (~5x)
claims.why: The measured CPU-bound speedups over Node for Go, Rust and the JVM are about 2–4x, which matches the claimed reduction to 5–10 of 20 minutes.

claims.claim: If the prototype uses headless Chromium, most of the 400 ms is spent inside Chromium, so a rewrite wouldn't touch that
claims.why: The benchmark doesn't measure Chromium or PDF rendering.

claims.claim: Budget roughly 100–300 MB per concurrent Chromium page
claims.why: The benchmark has no memory figures for Chromium.

claims.claim: Fly's shared-CPU machines have little headroom, so renders in worker threads would still squeeze the API
claims.about: Node worker threads on Fly shared-CPU machines
claims.why: The measurements use dedicated 1-CPU containers and don't cover Fly shared-CPU throttling or worker threads.
